original_abstract.text: We present LiRank, a large-scale ranking framework at LinkedIn that brings to production state-of-the-art modeling architectures and optimization methods. We unveil several modeling improvements, including Residual DCN, which adds attention and residual connections to the famous DCNv2 architecture. We share insights into combining and tuning SOTA architectures to create a unified model, including Dense Gating, Transformers and Residual DCN. We also propose novel techniques for calibration and describe how we productionalized deep learning based explore/exploit methods. To enable effective, production-grade serving of large ranking models, we detail how to train and compress models using quantization and vocabulary compression. We provide details about the deployment setup for large-scale use cases of Feed ranking, Jobs Recommendations, and Ads click-through rate (CTR) prediction. We summarize our learnings from various A/B tests by elucidating the most effective technical approaches. These ideas have contributed to relative metrics improvements across the board at LinkedIn: +0.5% member sessions in the Feed, +1.76% qualified job applications for Jobs search and recommendations, and +4.3% for Ads CTR. We hope this work can provide practical insights and solutions for practitioners interested in leveraging large-scale deep ranking systems.
original_abstract.source_title: LiRank: Industrial Large Scale Ranking Models at LinkedIn

en.text: LiRank reports a production ranking framework combining residual cross networks, Transformers and dense gating. It also covers calibration, exploration–exploitation and model compression through quantization and vocabulary reduction. Its contribution is the practical integration of modeling and deployment choices across several ranking tasks, rather than a single isolated interaction operator.

zh.text: LiRank 汇总残差交叉网络、Transformer 和稠密门控在生产排序中的组合方式，并讨论校准、探索与利用、量化和词表压缩。论文重点是这些建模与部署技术如何在不同排序任务中配合，形成可训练、可压缩、可上线的大规模系统。

original_abstract.text:
Large-scale recommendation systems are characterized by their reliance on high cardinality, heterogeneous features and the need to handle tens of billions of user actions on a daily basis. Despite being trained on huge volume of data with thousands of features, most Deep Learning Recommendation Models (DLRMs) in industry fail to scale with compute.
  Inspired by success achieved by Transformers in language and vision domains, we revisit fundamental design choices in recommendation systems. We reformulate recommendation problems as sequential transduction tasks within a generative modeling framework ("Generative Recommenders"), and propose a new architecture, HSTU, designed for high cardinality, non-stationary streaming recommendation data.
  HSTU outperforms baselines over synthetic and public datasets by up to 65.8% in NDCG, and is 5.3x to 15.2x faster than FlashAttention2-based Transformers on 8192 length sequences. HSTU-based Generative Recommenders, with 1.5 trillion parameters, improve metrics in online A/B tests by 12.4% and have been deployed on multiple surfaces of a large internet platform with billions of users. More importantly, the model quality of Generative Recommenders empirically scales as a power-law of training compute across three orders of magnitude, up to GPT-3/LLaMa-2 scale, which reduces carbon footprint needed for future model developments, and further paves the way for the first foundational models in recommendations.
original_abstract.source_title: Actions Speak Louder than Words: Trillion-Parameter Sequential Transducers for Generative Recommendations

en.text: HSTU reformulates recommendation as sequential transduction: a model learns from streams of user actions to produce recommendation-related outputs. Its architecture is designed for high-cardinality, heterogeneous and changing recommendation data rather than directly copying a language Transformer. The paper evaluates how this generative formulation scales with training compute and large-scale deployment.

zh.text: HSTU 将推荐改写为序列转换任务，让模型从用户行为流中学习并产生推荐相关输出。它针对类别基数大、特征异质且持续变化的数据设计网络结构，并研究这种生成式建模方式能否随着训练计算量增加持续改善效果，以及如何用于大规模线上系统。
